summary: Ozark County, MO: 40-acre towersite acquired 1953 and a tower erected 1953-54; Missouri Dept. of Conservation staff used it for fire detection per the 2015 plan.

facts.status_note: In use for fire detection per the 2015 plan and an undated Department site page; no source gives its condition since 2015.

staffing.status: Used for fire detection by Department staff (2015 plan; the Department's site page says the same)

access.note: Towersite open to the public per the 2015 plan; the access road is closed to vehicles when the tower is not manned. No source says the tower itself may be climbed

visit.trail_note: The 2015 plan lists no parking area for the site

events.note: Towersite acquired, 40 acres (area number 5307); fiscal 1952-53 report
New tower erected at Tecumseh (fiscal 1953-54 report); the sources read do not give its height or build type
Tower currently used for fire detection by Department staff (2015 plan)
The 2015 plan calls the towersite likely eligible for National Register of Historic Places listing (not listed)

notes_for_editor: Brief had no height, agency or ownership; height stays unset because the only readable sources give none. A Facebook post by the Missouri Conservation History page describes a 100-foot steel Aermotor tower, but the page was login-walled and was not used. Current condition is not confirmed beyond the 2015 plan and an undated MDC page. The 2015 plan's 'Date Acquired 1953' agrees with the Forest Lookouts page's fiscal 1952-53 entry. Visit.climbable and drive_up left unset: no source says whether the tower may be climbed or whether the site has a usable vehicle approach.
